column1: # Skeleton adjudication ledger — the VALIDITY gate. TAB-separated, 4 fields:
#   sentence <TAB> skeleton (sense-erased) <TAB> verdict <TAB> evidence
# Run `scripts/audit-skeletons.sh` to check coverage; it FAILS while anything is unadjudicated and
# writes a worksheet of the missing rows with `--worksheet`.
# WHY THIS EXISTS, SEPARATELY FROM expected-readings.tsv. That file gates FAITHFULNESS — the correct
# reading is still present — and says nothing about the other readings, so a unit can pass it while
# carrying invalid ones. Nothing checked those. An informal review of them on 2026-07-28 produced
# impressions rather than findings: it SAMPLED (`sort -u | head -6`) instead of enumerating, drifted
# between the two questions, and had no stated admissibility criterion, so "looks wrong" stood in for
# three different verdicts. One claim from that pass was wrong on inspection (the PARP-1 unit was
# called all-flat; 8 of its 10 readings are nested). This ledger is the correction: one row per
# skeleton, a verdict, and the evidence.
# VERDICTS — exactly one of:
#   correct    the intended reading. At most one per unit; it is also the pin.
#   available  structurally available and NOT the grammar's to refuse — semantically false, or true
#              but dispreferred. A PP that may attach high or low yields one `correct` and one
#              `available`. Ranking's problem.
#   invalid    the grammar should not produce it. Evidence MUST establish inadmissibility under EVERY
#              sense assignment, and name the rule that should block it. This is the defect backlog.
# The `available`/`invalid` line decides rule-change vs ranking-change, so argue over it. A merely
# false reading is `available`. The germline family qualified as `invalid` because "MSH6 causes Lynch
# syndrome" is false whether MSH6 denotes the gene or the protein — no sense assignment rescues it.
# Seeded 2026-07-28 with ONLY the verdicts established by evidence at the time; the remainder is
# deliberately left unadjudicated rather than bulk-filled, so the gate reports the real state.
# Skeleton strings are copied VERBATIM from the worksheet - a first attempt typed them by hand and all
# rows registered as stale, which is what the (unit, skeleton) key is for.
